display_name: Tyrrell's Vat 1 Semillon, New South Wales
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Defying the climate logic of its region, Hunter Valley Semillon relies on cloud cover during ripening to retain acidity despite the heat. Vat 1 remains the benchmark for how this variety transforms from lean citrus to complex toast over decades. This specific profile separates it from warmer climate whites that lose structure quickly.",
  "wine_summary": "Across extensive holdings in the Pokolbin subregion, sandy alluvial loam meets friable red duplex soils. These drainage profiles force vines to struggle, concentrating flavor without excessive sugar accumulation. The 2011 and 2015 vintages demonstrate the consistency of this site, delivering wines that start austere and develop beeswax and honey notes after five years in bottle.",
  "terroir_expression": "Because the region runs hot, cloud cover during the growing season moderates the intense New South Wales heat. Sandy alluvial loam provides drainage that limits vigor, while the underlying alkaline clay retains enough water to prevent shutdown during dry spells. This geological balance creates a wine with high natural acidity and a waxy texture that only emerges with time.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fermentation occurs in old oak barrels rather than stainless steel to allow slight oxygen exchange without imparting wood flavor. This micro-oxygenation helps stabilize the wine early while preserving primary fruit character. The winemaking team avoids malolactic fermentation to maintain the sharp malic acid structure necessary for long-term aging.",
  "food_pairing": "Raw oysters with mignonette work well because the high acid cuts through the brine.\nNashville hot chicken pairs effectively since the wine's lean profile cools the spice without sweetness.\nGrilled snapper with lemon butter matches the citrus notes and waxy texture.\nAged goat cheese tart complements the developing beeswax aromas in older vintages.\nTempura prawns stand up to the fried batter due to the crispness.",
  "comparable_wines": "Brokenwood Graveyard Semillon — similar Hunter Valley origin with slightly richer texture.\nMount Pleasant Elizabeth Semillon — another historic label with the same early-pick style.\nClare Valley Riesling (Grosset Polish Hill) — shares the high acid/low alcohol architecture but with different fruit profile.",
  "style_profile": "Semillon-based light-bodied dry white with piercing acidity and waxy texture.",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Store horizontally in a cool, dark space below 15°C to ensure longevity. Drink young for citrus zest or hold for 10+ years to see toast and honey development.",
  "value_assessment": "$60 places this above entry-level Australian whites but below luxury Bordeaux. Competitors like Brokenwood Graveyard often trade at similar levels depending on vintage availability. The cost is justified by an aging trajectory that outperforms most whites at this price point.",
  "market_position": "Collectors target specific vintages like 2007 or 2011 for vertical tastings. Restaurant lists feature younger releases alongside aged library bottles to show the variety's range. Casual drinkers often overlook this label due to the lean profile in youth, preferring more overtly fruity options.",
  "insider_take": "Many buyers reject young Vat 1 because it tastes too lean and acidic upon release. Patience is required; the wine needs at least five years to integrate and show its true capacity. Skip this if you prefer immediate tropical fruit bomb styles.",
  "aging_potential_years": 20,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 5,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 25,

}

parsed.hook: Defying the climate logic of its region, Hunter Valley Semillon relies on cloud cover during ripening to retain acidity despite the heat. Vat 1 remains the benchmark for how this variety transforms from lean citrus to complex toast over decades. This specific profile separates it from warmer climate whites that lose structure quickly.
parsed.wine_summary: Across extensive holdings in the Pokolbin subregion, sandy alluvial loam meets friable red duplex soils. These drainage profiles force vines to struggle, concentrating flavor without excessive sugar accumulation. The 2011 and 2015 vintages demonstrate the consistency of this site, delivering wines that start austere and develop beeswax and honey notes after five years in bottle.
parsed.terroir_expression: Because the region runs hot, cloud cover during the growing season moderates the intense New South Wales heat. Sandy alluvial loam provides drainage that limits vigor, while the underlying alkaline clay retains enough water to prevent shutdown during dry spells. This geological balance creates a wine with high natural acidity and a waxy texture that only emerges with time.
parsed.vinification_summary: Fermentation occurs in old oak barrels rather than stainless steel to allow slight oxygen exchange without imparting wood flavor. This micro-oxygenation helps stabilize the wine early while preserving primary fruit character. The winemaking team avoids malolactic fermentation to maintain the sharp malic acid structure necessary for long-term aging.
parsed.food_pairing:
Raw oysters with mignonette work well because the high acid cuts through the brine.
Nashville hot chicken pairs effectively since the wine's lean profile cools the spice without sweetness.
Grilled snapper with lemon butter matches the citrus notes and waxy texture.
Aged goat cheese tart complements the developing beeswax aromas in older vintages.
Tempura prawns stand up to the fried batter due to the crispness.
parsed.comparable_wines:
Brokenwood Graveyard Semillon — similar Hunter Valley origin with slightly richer texture.
Mount Pleasant Elizabeth Semillon — another historic label with the same early-pick style.
Clare Valley Riesling (Grosset Polish Hill) — shares the high acid/low alcohol architecture but with different fruit profile.
